audit.whatIsWrong: 'W any dash he tries — his mobility is a suggestion' — Trundle has no dash, which the early paragraph itself already admits. Chomp was never identified as an auto-attack reset, and the sap was left vague ('shreds your HP' in the TL;DR) when it saps attack damage.
audit.why: The auto-reset is the burst tell: the wind-up, not the cast, is the cue to step back. And Frozen Domain increases healing from all sources while he stands on it, which is what actually punishes a long trade.
audit.corrected: W line replaced with the real reason to keep trades short; Chomp named as a 3.5s auto reset that saps attack damage; Frozen Domain named as the healing zone.

audit.corrected: Written into dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and the mid paragraph.

edits.before: Keep trades SHORT. The moment he bites you with Q he steals your AD and slows you, turning a long fight in his favor, so commit your E-wall-stun + Q combo, deal your chunk, and disengage before his lifesteal catches up. At 6 your R is for safety, not a kill — use it to cancel his pillar-trap all-in or fling him away from you, never to chase a drain-tank who heals as he fights. Your first item of cheap bruiser components keeps you ahead of his pre-R sustain.
edits.after: Keep trades SHORT. Chomp is an auto-attack reset on a flat 3.5s — the wind-up is your cue to step back, not the cast — and it saps your attack damage as it slows. Commit the E-wall-stun into Q, take the chunk, and leave before Frozen Domain's boosted healing catches up. Have Grievous Wounds on him before any long fight: King's Tribute heals him off every unit that dies nearby. At 6 your R is safety, not a kill — fling him off you, never chase a drain-tank.
